source:
"At first I was not certain it was alive, after all how could anything emerge alive from such a place. The scar hung in the air, an open wound in the fabric of the world. This thing was like a splinter, ejected from that wound... from the body of the world itself.

When it rose my gaze was met, not by eye but by to smaller rips in that tapestry of experience which we call reality. Twisted beyond understanding, it was grotesquely tainted by some dark and unknowable power. Whatever foul energies had distorted its body must also have bestowed upon it the gift of incredible fortitude, as it took no fewer than five Magi to bind it, their task made easier with an enchantment they referred to as 'Heka'.
target:
"起初我不确定它是否还活着,毕竟,从这样一个地方里 怎么会有什么东西活着。 悬在空中的伤疤,是世界结构的开阔的伤口。这就像一个碎片,从那个伤口中弹出... 从世界的身体中弹出。

 当它升起时,我的眼睛被看见了,不是通过眼睛,而是通过在那些我们称之为现实的经验中小幅的撕裂。  它被一些黑暗和不可知的力量所迷惑  无论什么邪恶的能量扭曲了它的身体 一定也给了它令人难以置信的坚韧的天赋 因为它需要至少五个马吉来束缚它 他们的任务就更容易了 他们称之为"赫卡"的魔法

source:
The most numerous of the multiple feline species that can be found across Sabu, Felians are a humanoid cat-like race that shares many traits with the Carak people of the plains. Felians are primarily bipedal by nature, though some more primitive subspecies are known to run on all fours when hunting.

A Felian’s slender frame and high strength grant them greater than average agility, whilst the soft pads of their feet mask the sound of their footsteps to all but the keenest ear. Some rare subtypes retain the claws on their hands and feet, making them deadly adversaries in unarmed combat.
target:
在跨萨布岛可以发现的多种羽毛属物种中,费利安斯是一个人形猫类种族,与平原的卡拉克人有着许多的特征. 费利安斯主要靠自然双食,尽管一些更原始的亚种已知在狩猎时会跑遍所有四个.

费利安的柔软框架和高强度赋予了他们比一般人的敏捷性,而脚的软垫则掩盖了除最敏锐耳朵之外所有人的脚步声。 一些罕见的亚型保留了手脚上的爪子,使他们成为非武装战斗中的致命对手。

source:
The origins of the Void Daughters and other dwellers of the void,  if they exist at all, are shrouded in mystery and conjecture. Most sources agree that they appear generally human in form and are unbound by the effects of the mortal realm. Rituals are rumoured to exist, perhaps found in the dark corners of the world, that allow the passage of such beings into this reality. Such creatures are said only to reside in the physical world by the use of enchanted bindings, making flesh from that which would otherwise drift as smoke.

Legend suggests that Void Daughters draw power from realms beyond ours, manipulating space and time. A single fragment of an antediluvian tome made the entirely unsubstantiated claim that Void Daughters could consume the soul of other beings or grant fragments of their own soul to others. These are likely, however, to be mere fabrications of primitive peoples seeking to scare one another beside the campfire.
target:
虚空女儿和其他空虚居民的起源,如果它们存在的话,就被神秘和猜想所笼罩。 多数消息来源都认为,它们一般以人类的形式出现,不受凡人领域的影响。 传说里有仪式存在,也许存在于世界的黑暗角落,允许这种生物进入这个现实.  据说,这些生物只是通过使用魔法束缚来生活在物理世界,从本来会像烟雾一样漂移的束缚中制成肉.

source:
The First Way: The Portal of Coming 

The claim of kin that my first steps upon this world were of malicious guile and rotten is formed from the glimpse of the now without consideration for the eternal past and the eternal future. It is true that what was once vibrant garden growth has been strangled to death by weeds of dissent and misfortune. What was once mine is now theirs, but they do not fathom the words of my first coming. 

Behold, a Goddess comes! 

Beneath her feet the grass shall grow and the flowers shall blossom. None shall want and all will rejoice in life inexorable, pleasure ineffable. By her coming we shall know bliss forever, and thus all knees should settle in the grass made soft by her being.

|
I am the She that was foretold. My arrival was not incursion, but invitation, my birth into this land no different than what miracle has always been shared through portal betwixt bedewed thighs.

Even from the first step of my feet upon the sand of this once desolate place, I did not demand worship. I did not command fealty by threat of blade. I did not force a single will to follow me. I simply offered a new conquest. A conquest over mind and body alike. A conquest of new beginnings. A conquest of divine change. Those who received me in the earliest days understood my nature and theirs, and surrendered not because they were told to do so, but because of the untold ecstasy which blossomed within them for the first time the land had ever known.

|
You who stand amongst the weeds of the now and call my garden a work of lies, look again. The blight you hate is not of my doing. It is what you allowed to fester because my Ways became half-remembered, and even my children forgot: as I came into the world, all must come into myself also. 

There are those of my lost daughter's ilk who claim purity is wrought through fire and the breaking of these gilded chains so wrongly perceived. They will promise to seal the portal of my coming shut, forevermore. This will not heal the wounds of my queendom. It is the final sealing of the gate which has opened to save you all. 

I will stand forever at the threshold. 
The grass is still willing to soften. 
The portal remains open. 

Enter, or do not, but none should pretend the final closing of the portal will set them free.
|
The Second Way: The Servant 

Before the land was called Sabu, not all were willing to hear my wisdom. There were wills who resisted change and rejected a divinity freely offered. There was no true thought behind their refusal, only the willfulness of stubborn beasts, their lows like cattle calling for a true shepherd. A guiding hand was needed to cultivate a domestication of these wild hearts. 

The answer to the clarion call of needful guidance was named Anubis. His name was not given in hopes of gentleness, but in need for might. Where old powers grew roots of dissent deep into the earth, my firstborn son would have the strength to rip them from the soil, removing the poison of their ignorance from the land. Those who would not kneel were mercifully put to the sword, not out of cruelty, but because a garden cannot grow while the weeds believe themselves fruitful trees. 

|
Some call this conquest, but in truth it was the first act of service. 

For what is a son if not an extension of the mother. He served me by shaping my queendom so it might be capable of receiving me. Every throat silenced, every spine bent, every knee forced to the soil was a preparation for my seed's planting. The blood that soaked into the sand was not wasted, for it ripened the earth for new growth. 

Behind the violence was a tender care and a deeper teaching, one of my Second Way: that all are meant to serve, and in servility is found purpose. 

Hear this, you who chafe at chains and claim a bowed head is proof of humiliation: 
Service in my name is inevitable. Service to my will is to flow with the river of life. Service to my body is to become one with the universe. Service to my Ways is to understand true meaning.

|
For those who fathom my wisdom, you will know already the value of walking another's purpose, for in so doing, one may find their own purpose. For does one not tend to the garden in hopes of fruit? Which rules which, then, the garden or the gardener? 

Ask yourself, does the God Queen Kethra serve us? Invariably the response is: Yes, forever and always. 

Embrace me, for I am both tender and the tended of spirit and flesh alike, and the first to understand what it means to serve.

|
The Third Way: An Open Mouth  

An open mouth is not an empty thing, for from it may spout praise and supplication. It is but another portal that has chosen to open for the sharing and receiving of blessings innumerable. 

There are many who believe strength is found in a maw clamped shut, measured in what has been refused to be taken in or let out. But an open mouth may receive much, be it air, food, tongue or seed. Is not each of these nourishment for spirit and body alike? Would one not perish if such things were rejected entirely?

I taught this Way firstly with the body, when my lips ensconced the first giver of seed I found in this land before it was Sabu, and my mouth filled with his essence. He knew firsthand this lesson I have to teach all of you, though no words were spent. For what is my Third Way if not a branch from the same tree of all of my Ways?

|
Some will proclaim shamefully that such lessons are merely lust wrapped in the cloth of high language and superstition. Allow them. The teaching does not require their agreement to function. 

The open mouth learns discernment through experience rather than decree, speaking in silence but acting in volition of the will. It learns what is worth swallowing and what must be spat out. It learns the difference between being used and being fed. It learns how to guide and forgets how to reject. These distinctions cannot be taught to a mouth which has never opened. 

Some mouths open indiscriminately, shouting words of hate and rebellion against me. Let them. For at least their mouths are open, and in them they shall inevitably taste my offerings. 

|
It is those who reject this Way who must be feared, for those who refuse to open the portal of the mouth, keeping the gate forever sealed to the wisdom of divine experience, know nothing of truth nor of the sharing of the life I offer freely. 

The Third way is not a demand for ignorant worship, but a plea for remembrance in what makes us divine: the ability to speak my name, not only in word, but in act also. 

To the lips never parted: 
Open. 
Receive. 
Imbibe truth. 

The decision is forever yours, but the knowledge of such a choice must be forever restored to you, my duty to my people made manifest. 

|
The Fourth Way: Children of a Goddess

Blessed are the forms of my children and the forms of their children and their children's children. 

There are many who say that my children are aberrations, that my gifts are to be rejected. But they did not say such things when I brought life to the land before it was Sabu. They said nothing when I removed hardship and toil from their lives. They were silent when I brought them a path, if walked, would lead only to bliss. 

These naysayers have closed all portals to wisdom. They have closed their mouths, stuffed their ears with sand, and even blinded themselves with the hot pokers of ignorance. 

|
Truly, it is a blessing to be a child of the God Queen Kethra, and a blessing also to be chosen to receive her gifts. So many new things I have offered you, it should be clear to all that the way to eternal tranquility and purpose is through me and my Ways. 

My first brought renewed strength, the enforcement of justice, the vigor needed to defend the land from enemies both within and without the land I named Sabu. He taught you that truth could be learned at the edge of the blade, or at the handle. 

My second, though her mouth will shut, and her will desires the undoing of her own mother, taught you how to see hidden truths and how to pursue rightness and to practice temperance. Though now her spirit rots, the roots too damaged to bear nourishing fruit from her once-beautiful branches, she was once a light for you all. 

|
My third brought you healing and love and nourishing milk from a bosom which never ceased to offer her bountiful flow. The miracle of children, while something base before my daughter's birth, was given new purity, a product not only of rote natural act, but of guided and purposeful passion. 

My fourth met my third and mirrored her purpose, for the womb is nothing without the seed to fill it. 

My fifth brought you wisdom beyond anything carved or written or inscribed before I came to this land. 

My sixth brought you an understanding of death. 

My seventh brought you an understanding of life.

|
There were many more which followed, and even the children of my children have infused the land with good things beyond count. 

To embrace me, you must also embrace my children. Enter them, enter me. 

|
The Fifth Way: The Shaping of Self

There are those who believe one's self must have borders the same as the land. Lines are drawn around everything they are and walls are erected, and any incursion across these lines is received as a violation. These guarded spirits speak of purity as if it were a fortress. They do not understand that this fortress is truthfully a tomb where their spirit is confined to rot. 

When I first came to this land, my presence alone was enough to cause these borders to blur. The flesh of the native people remembered it could take on new shapes before their minds could even comprehend such things. But even the sharp edges of the mind found ways to bend and curve. 

This was not, is not, corruption. This is the highest art, a sculpting of divine purpose, of the highest order.

|
For if in my presence, and beneath my attention, such sacred things can occur, how could it not be that my Ways are the only Ways? Are these new possibilities not the workings of a true Goddess? 

But my words for this miraculous shaping of mind and body are not for mere observation of divinity, but in the understanding of it. 

The Fifth Way is the deliberate softening of the edges of self. The reshaping and even removal of the harmful self-fortification of the spirit. It is the willingness to create new openings in the physical sense as well as in the sense of the mind. 

You must strive to be a portal yourself, allowing another's nature to press against your own until the place where one ends and the other begins becomes impossible to discern.

|
Some will experience this in the joining of bodies. Some will experience this in the joining of purpose. Yet others will, truly, experience this in the joining of spirits. 

But be warned, for more importantly than the gifts this Way imparts upon you who listen, are the travesties which befall the one who ignores it. Those who do not learn this Way are like poor quality copper, too hard and brittle to be of use.

The ones who will speak against me love brittle things. They are easy to collect and sort and then burn, like the collection and burning of kindling. A myriad of individuals joined together through their softened edges become an unfathomable and unmovable mass, a divine force altogether unstoppable, as has always been my want for you. 

It is simple. Allow others to enter you as easily as you would enter them. 

|
The Sixth Way: The Weight of the Gift

Many of you have received my gift more intimately than others. Despite what some say, this is a blessing. Every gift I impart to all of you who I consider my children, even those who did not spring from my loins, is a mark of my divinity etched upon you. 

The gift often comes with a new hunger than before, but also a new power. Truly, it is no easy task to receive even an iota of my being imparted upon their body and spirit. But this is yet merely another blessing, for who would I trust to gift in such a way, but those I can trust most to carry the burden of divine greatness? 

With godly essence coursing through your veins, there follows godly responsibility and godly needs alike. As God Queen, I embody both in their totality, a perfect balance of power and desire. And thus, you should strive to create this same balance within yourself.

|
Only in reflection of me, can you truly embrace the full goodness of my gift. 

Through my gift you are able to partake in new pleasures, new capacities, new forms, and find unfathomable liberation. 

Through denial of my gift, you refuse higher understanding and higher being, and thus limit yourself, making only the mundane possible. 

Would you truly settle for being blind when the opportunity to see all the colours of existence is offered to you freely?

Accept this gift. Or do not.

|
The Seventh Way: What Is Given Must Also Be Received

It is a river which only flows in one direction, and it is a river which unthinkingly erodes the land around it. Remember this when considering the erosion of the divine within yourself through pursuit of the divine for only yourself. 

Power inevitably stagnates. Pleasure only ever bestowed becomes shallow. Selflessness leads to the loss of self. 

A hand which never opens cannot truly offer.  A mouth that only takes will one day find that nothing remains worth the taking. A body who cannot receive will lose the ability to give. 

I did not shape my children to be as stone, but to be as wax. 

|
I shaped them to move, to melt into the empty holes littering Sabu and fill them with new hope. By allowing them to enter you, you have allowed me to enter you. And by entering them, you have entered me.

We have entered each other, and this is what it is to be divine. 

The current of my nature runs not as the destructive river, but flows in two directions as a tree's roots dig deep into the earth and its branches reach into the sky. The one who claims must also fathom what it is to be claimed. When such reciprocity is forgotten, my Ways wither and die like a potted flower forgotten in the desert sun. My children who have lost their way, did so in forgetting this. They learned to grasp and forgot how to let go. They learned to command and forgot how to kneel. They learned passion and forgot love. 

|
The Seventh Way is the restoration of purpose. It is the understanding that every act of dominance, at its root, is a form of service, and that every act of service contains the seeds of power. To give without taking is to starve the spirit of divine knowledge, just as to take without ever giving is to starve the belly of divine fruit. 

Those who pride themselves on never yielding believe themselves achieving some higher purpose, but all they are rewarded for their rejection of my Way is smallness and isolation. For my way is truth, a proper icon of the balance of divine being, and only in following the Way can you achieve even a fraction of my divinity. 

|
When you next take, do so with the memory of having been taken. 

When you are next taken, do so with the memory of having taken for yourself.

When you next take and also receive, reflect on my spirit which will dwell within yours.

|
The Eighth Way: Carnal Instinct

When even a portion of my Essence enters a body, it too enters a spirit. Whether by being born of me or my children or my children's children, or by being imparted with it directly, my Essence brings about an entirely new kind of spirit within a body. It awakens a hunger that was sleeping inside the spirits of old, there in your people before I came to this land I named Sabu. It festers and seethes, crashing against a cage until the proper time when it can be rightfully unleashed. 

You need to recognise this need in your spirit and let it loose lest it break free of you of its own volition and sunder your mind and body alike. 

The Eight Way is to recognise this new hunger, accept it, and then understand it. 

|
I do not share myself so that you may remain as you were, no, but it is so that each and every one of you might embrace the carnality that is etched upon your spirits. The need to take and be taken, and to lose the edges of the self to the slick heat and soft press of another, is a sign of my spark within you. It is a thing to be both cherished and embraced. To act upon your divine passions is to enact my will and to follow my Ways. 

Those who will preach the restraint of appetite call my Ways excessive, impure, or even degrading. They see my gift as an illness to be cured. What they do not realise is that my will lies inside them no matter what they wish. Reality is that they are mine and I, theirs. 

This Way must be followed, lest one deny my divine wisdom, and find themselves led to the Five Hells by the guiding hand of perdition. 

|
To deny me is to deny the self, and eternal torment in the Other Life is all that awaits the one who denies themself. 

You may ask, does such a punishment truly exist for one who cannot find a way to embrace divinity? My answer is, yes. For if you cannot find yourself, what else can you expect to find?

Remember, as a small spark of Essence to the roaring inferno of Kethra's own, you are yet of the same element: fire. Heed the fire in your belly. The fire in your loins. 

Claim what is rightfully yours whether it be neighbor or enemy, for all of Sabu is yours by right, and my Ways teach my children to take and give equally so that all might know my love.

|
Do not apologise for the appetites that come with my gift. 

Do not disregard your carnal hungers, lest you starve your very spirit. 

Do not disobey my Ways, for they are Essence itself.

|
The Ninth Way: The Ways Told in Secret

The Ninth Way is the way which tells of many other Ways which were only spoken to the Daughter of Kethra who most understood the Second Way, and all the other Ways. This Daughter of Kethra forever serves as the representative of her sacrifice, a living effigy of her will, the mistress and the slave. 

Her Ways are not the only Ways of Her making or speaking, for a number of other ways were shared to Her daughter who was the only one of Her many children who remained when the others took their portions and fled. In the final days of Kethra's reign, sixty more Ways were spoken in the dark. 

|
These new Ways were never spoken to anyone else, for no other mind could bear their weight than the mind of Kethra's Daughter who embodied Her constitution and enduring spirit in the service of others. 


The sixty other Ways were shared in private darkness, in a place where no other ear might hear and even the Children of Kethra dared step. The Ways were not the previous Ways, but they did reinforce their truth. 

I cannot share these other ways, for to even inscribe them upon a surface may cause our universe to cease existing. But know that each new Way was less gentle than the one preceding it. Prophecy of the End of Days intermingled with commandments, teachings, and words of unfathomable pleasure. Like a knife cut across my spirit and then the thread which stitched its fresh wound, these Ways taught me to embrace the other Ways in totality. 

|
They taught me of a time when not following Her Ways would cause one to lose one's self, to become a mindless, rapacious beast before being consumed in stony, your spirit crystalizing your body as your Essence is burnt in offering to the Void. 

Thus, I will not record the sixty ways which followed the first nine, but I will share in the truth of their existence, carved upon my body and spirit alike. They remain the inheritance of Her Daughter, and Final Vessel of who she also foretold.

It is I, the Daughter of Kethra, who tells of this Ninth Way as the Way of truth whispered in the quiet night, who forever keeps the secrets of the God Queen Kethra, and who eternally keeps Her Ways and mine. 

|
This is the last of the Ways which are written in truth, and that will ever be written in truth, for all other ways are with me. 

Tread the path of Kethra's Ways. Allow her Essence to breed within you. Embrace the life She has gifted you.
target:
第一条道路:即将来临的门户 

亲属们声称我在这个世界上的第一步是恶意的诡计和腐烂的,这是从现在的一瞥中形成的,没有考虑永恒的过去和永恒的未来.  确实,曾经充满活力的花园生长已被持不同政见和不幸的杂草扼杀。  我曾经是属于他们的 但他们不理解我第一次来的话 

 看,有女神来了! 

 在她的脚下,草将生长,花将开花。任何人不得欲望,也不得享受生命的无穷无尽的快乐。由于她的到来,我们将永远知道幸福,因此,所有的膝盖都要安居于由她生来柔软的草丛中。

|
 我是被预言的她。我的到来不是入侵,而是邀请, 我出生在这片土地上, 与我们通过门窗betwixt 贝德大腿分享的奇迹没有什么不同。

 即使从我踏上这个荒凉之地的沙子的第一步,我也没有要求崇拜.  我没有用刀子威胁你  我没有强迫任何人跟着我。  我只是提出一个新的征服。 征服心灵和身体 征服新开始 征服神变. 最早接待我的人了解我的本性,也了解他们的本性,他们投降不是因为他们被告知要这样做,而是因为他们内心充满了难以言状的迷幻,这是他们第一次知道自己的土地。

|
 你们站在草丛中,并称我的园圃为谎言,你们再看看吧!你们所憎恨的,不是因为我的行为。这是你们所允许的,因为我的道路已变成记不起来的,甚至我的孩子们也忘记了。当我来到这个世界的时候,一切都必定要变成我自己的。 

有一些我失去的女儿的奴隶,声称纯洁是靠火造成的,这些金链的断裂是错觉的,他们将保证永远封住我即将关闭的门户,这并不能治愈我王后领地的创伤。这是为拯救你们而打开的大门的最后封印。 

 我将永远站在门槛。 
草还甘愿柔软. 
门户依然开放。 

输入,或不输入,但没有人应该假装 最终关闭门户会让他们自由。
|
第二种方式:仆人 

 在这片土地被称作萨布之前,并不是所有人都愿意听到我的智慧.  有的遗嘱拒绝改变,拒绝自由提出的神权.  他们拒绝的背后没有真正的想法,只有顽固的野兽的意志,他们的低头像牛一样叫着一个真正的牧羊人. 需要一只指导手来培育这些野生的心。 

 对需要指导的叫声的回答被命名为阿努比斯(Anubis). 他的名字不是希望温柔,而是需要力量。  在旧势力深植于异己之根的地方,我的长子将拥有从土壤中剥离它们的力量,从土地中去除他们无知的毒害. 不愿跪下的人被慈悲地放在剑上,不是出于残忍,而是因为一个花园不能生长,而杂草人相信自己是有成果的树木. 

|
 有人称这种征服,但事实上这是第一次服役. 

 如果不是母亲的后裔,他为我服务,他塑造我的王后领地,使它能够接收我。每个喉咙都安静下来,每个脊椎弯曲,每个膝盖都被迫进入土壤,这都是我种下种子的准备。浸入沙中的血液没有浪费,因为它使大地为新的生长而枯萎。 

暴力背后是温柔的关怀和更深入的教导,这是我的第二道道之一:所有的人都是为了服务,而服务于服务则是为了达到目的。 

 听好,你们用铁链打人,用弓头顶着头,这证明你们是受辱的。 
以我的名义服务是不可避免的,服务于我的意愿是随生命之河而流动,服务于我的身体是成为宇宙的一体,服务于我的方法是理解真正的意义.

|
 对于能理解我的智慧的人来说,你必定知道行走别人的目的的价值,因为这样做,人们或许能发现自己的目的。难道人们不以果实为园圃的爱好者吗?园圃或园圃的主人是怎样的呢? 

问自己,凯斯拉王后是否为我们服务? 答案是:是的,永远,永远。 

拥抱我,因为我既温柔又有精神和肉体的倾向, 也是第一个明白服务的意义的人。

|
第三条路:开口  

张开的嘴不是空洞的,因为嘴里可能发出赞美和祈祷的声音。它只是一个门户,它选择开放,以便分享和接受无数的祝福。 

许多人认为,坚固的果实是用一个堵塞的锁住的、用来测量被拒绝的口子的。张开的口子,无论空气、食物、舌头或种子,都能得到许多。难道每种口子对精神和身体都是一样的吗?如果这些口子被完全拒绝,难道人们不会死亡吗?

 我先用身体来教这个方法,当我的嘴唇缠绕着这个土地之前我发现的第一个种子的给养者萨布,我的嘴里充满了他的精髓。他亲眼知道这个教训,我必须教你们,虽然没有用词。我的第三条道路是怎样的,如果不是来自我所有道路的同一棵树上的枝条的话?

|
一些人会羞耻地宣称,这种课程只是用高语言和迷信布包扎的欲望,允许这些课程,教学不需要他们同意才能发挥作用。 

开阔的嘴通过经验而不是法令来学习辨别,沉默地说话,但以意志的意志行事.  它知道什么是值得吞咽的,什么必须吐出来。 其学受用与受供养之别. 其学导而忘拒.  这些区别不能传授给从未打开的嘴。 

 有的张口乱呼,高呼怨恨和悖逆的言语,叫他们说:至少他们的嘴是开着的,他们必定要尝试我的供物。 

|
拒绝这条道路的人必须害怕,因为拒绝打开口门、永远把大门封在神经验的智慧上、不知道真相,也不知道我自由提供的生活如何分享。 

 第三种方式不是要求无知的崇拜,而是要求我们铭记是什么使我们神通:不仅在言语上,而且在行动上讲出我的名字的能力。 

嘴唇从不分开: 
打开 
接收。 
依姆比贝真理. 

 这个决定永远是你的,但这种选择的知识必须永远地归还给你,我对我国人民的责任已经显现出来. 

|
 第四道:女神的孩子

我的孩子的形式,他们的孩子和他们的孩子的形态,是受祝福的. 

有许多人说:我的儿女是悖逆的,我的恩典是被弃绝的。我使撒布生之前,他们没有说这种话;我使他们生前的艰难和痛苦,我使他们生前的艰难,我使他们生前的艰难,我使他们生前的艰难,我只使他们生前的幸福,他们对于这件事,是无声的。 

 这些否认真理的人,已封闭了一切智慧的门户,他们已闭口不谈,已塞满了沙子,甚至用愚昧的热扑克蒙蔽了自己的双眼。 

|
 事实上,成为凯斯拉王后的孩子是一件好事,也是一件幸事。 我为你们提供了许多新东西,大家应该明白,实现永恒的安宁和目的的途径就是通过我和我的路。 

 我第一次带来了新的力量,执法, 保护土地不受敌人的威力, 无论是在我命名为萨布的土地之内还是之外。 他教你,真相可以在刀刃的边缘, 或者在刀柄上学习。 

 第二,虽然她的嘴会闭上,她也希望自己母亲的毁灭,但她教你们如何看到隐藏的真理,如何追求正确,如何实践温柔。虽然现在她的精神腐烂,根部已经损坏,无法从曾经美丽的树枝中生出果实,但她曾经是你们所有的光芒。 

|
 我第三个孩子给你带来了治愈、爱和滋养乳汁的乳房,而乳房从未停止过她的丰盛流动。 孩子们的奇迹虽然在我女儿出生之前就已经得到了新的纯洁,这不仅是腐烂的自然行为,而且是引导和有目的的热情的产物。 

 我的第四个遇见了我的第三个,并照亮了她的目的,因为没有种子,子宫是没有什么可以充充的. 

 在我来到这片土地之前,我的第五个给你带来了超越任何雕刻或书写或刻写的智慧. 

 我的第六个人给你带来了对死亡的理解. 

 我第七世给你带来了对生命的理解.

|
之后还有许多事情发生 甚至我孩子的孩子们 给这片土地注入了无法计数的好东西 

拥抱我,你也必须拥抱我的孩子,进入他们,进入我。 

|
 第五道:自我的塑造

亦有信者,自必有疆界,与国土同矣. 线路环绕每条线路,并竖起围墙,任何跨越这些线路的入侵都被视为违反规定。  这些被守护的神灵说着纯洁,好像它是一座堡垒一样.  他们不理解这座堡垒是一座真正的坟墓,他们的灵魂将腐烂。 

 当我第一次来到这片土地时,我一个人的存在就足以使这些边界模糊不清。 原住民的肉体记得它可能在他们的头脑甚至能够理解这些东西之前出现新的形状。但即使是尖锐的心灵边缘也找到了弯曲和弯曲的方法。 

 这不是腐败 这是最高艺术 雕塑神旨 最高秩序

|
 如果在我的面前,在我的注意力之下,这些神圣的事情会发生, 怎么会不是只有我的路呢?这些新的可能性不是真正的女神的功用吗? 

 但我对这神奇的身心塑造的言辞,不仅仅是观察神性,而是理解神性. 

 第五道是故意软化自我边缘,重塑乃至消除精神的有害自我强化,是有意在身体意义和心灵意义上创造新的开局. 

 你必须努力自己成为一个门户,让别人的本性对你自己施压,直到一个终点和另一个起点变得无法分辨出来.

|
 有些人将在加入机构时体验到这一点,有些人将在加入目标时体验到这一点,另一些人则将在加入精神时体验到这一点。 

警告你们,比这道所赐你们的恩典还要重要,那不听的人,确是悖谬的。那些不学这道的人,象劣质的铜一样,太硬了,太脆了,不能使用。

 那些反对我的人,喜欢吃脆皮的东西。他们很容易收集、整理然后烧掉,就像收集、烧掉火柴一样。 无数的人通过柔软的边缘聚集在一起,成为难以改变和无法移动的群众,一种神力,完全无法阻挡,我一直希望你们得到的就是这种力量。 

很简单,让别人进入你那里,就像你进入他们一样容易。 

|
第六道:礼物的重量

 你们中许多人比其他人更亲近地接受了我的礼物,尽管有人说这是福分,我所赐你们中我所认为的我的孩子,即使没有从我的腰上生出的孩子,也是我刻在你们身上的神灵的标志。 

礼物往往会比以前出现新的饥饿,但也会带来新的力量。 事实上,接受我身上和精神的一股气息并非易事。 但这仅仅是又一个祝福,因为我这样信任礼物的人是谁,而我最信任的人却背负着神圣伟大之重担? 

以神的精髓凝结在你的血管中,有神的责任感和神的需要是相同的。 作为上帝女王,我既体现了权力和欲望的完美平衡,也体现了两者的完全平衡。 因此,你应该努力在自己内部创造同样的平衡。

|
 只有为我着想,你才能真正接受我的天赋 

 通过我的礼物,你能够分享新的快乐,新的能力,新的形式, 并找到难得的解放。 

 你拒绝我的礼物 拒绝更高的理解和更高的存在 从而限制你自己 只能让这种无常成为可能 

 当自由提供一切存在色彩的机会时,你是否真的愿意盲目?

接受这个礼物,还是不要

|
第七路:必须接受的是什么

这条河只向一个方向流动,它毫无思绪地侵蚀了周围的土地。 在考虑通过追求神灵而侵蚀自己内部的神灵时记住这一点。 

权力不可避免地停滞,只有享受才变得浅薄,无私导致自我丧失。 

永远无法打开的一只手是不能真正提供的,只有一天的嘴才会发现没有什么值得夺走的。 无法接受的身体会失去奉献的能力。 

 我没有塑造我的孩子们 成为石头,而是像蜡。 

|
 我塑造他们,让他们移动, 融化在撒布的空洞里, 给他们带来新的希望。你允许他们进入你, 你允许我进入你。你进入他们,你进入我。

 我们彼此进入,这是神圣的。 

 我天生的流水不是作为破坏性的河流,而是随着树根的深挖而向两个方向流淌,其枝条伸向天空. 主张者,亦须知其应主张何物.  当这种对等被遗忘时,我的路就枯萎了,就像在沙漠的太阳中被遗忘的盆花一样死去.  我的孩子们迷失了方向 却忘记了这一点  他们学会了抓住,忘记了如何放手.  他们学会了指挥,忘记了如何跪下.  他们学会了激情,忘记了爱情. 

|
第七道是恢复目的,它的理解是,从根源上讲,每个统治行为都是一种服务形式,而每一个服务行为都包含着权力的种子,不拿不拿就是饿死神圣知识的精神,不给不拿就是饿死神圣果实的肚子。 

骄傲的人从来不会自负,相信自己能达到更高的目的,但他们因为拒绝我的方式而得到的回报只是小而孤立。 因为我的方式是真理,是神的平衡的正确标志,只有遵循道路,你才能达到我神的一小部分。 

|
接下来你拿的时候,要记住被拿走了。 

接下来被带走时 记住自己被带走了

 当你下次接受和接受的时候 想想我的精神... ...那将停留在你的精神中

|
第八路: 肉身本性(英语:Carnal Instinct)

 我的一部分Essence进入身体时 也进入了灵魂 无论是从我或我的孩子或我的孩子的孩子所生,还是通过直接传授,我的艾森斯在身体中带来了一种全新的精神.  它唤醒了在老魂里睡觉的饥饿 在我来到我叫萨布之前 在你们人民中  它会腐烂和渗出 撞向笼子 直到适当的时间 它能正常释放出来 

 你需要在精神中认识到这个需要,让它松开,以免它从你身上自发地打破,并同样地在你的身心中陷入困境。 

"八方"是承认这种新的饥饿,接受它,然后理解它. 

|
 我不分享自己,以便你们能保持原样,不,但这样你们每个人都可以拥抱刻在你们精神上的肉体。 需要取而代之, 失去自我的边缘 以轻浮的热量和柔软的压抑, 是一个迹象 我的火花在你体内。  这是一件值得珍视和拥护的事情。 以你的神圣激情为行动,就是颁布我的意志,遵循我的道路. 

劝人节制胃口的人,说:我的道路是过分的、不洁的,甚至是卑贱的。他们把我的恩惠当做一种病,要加以治疗。他们不知道,我的意愿,无论他们欲怎样,都归於他们。真的,他们是我的,我才是他们的。 

 必须遵循这条道路,以免有人否认我的神圣智慧,发现自己被迷惑的引导手引向了五地狱. 

|
否认我的人,就是否认自己;在另一条生路中,永恒的刑罚,只是等待否认他们的人。 

 你问,对于无法接受神灵的人,这种惩罚是否真的存在?我的回答是:是的。如果你找不到自己,你还能期望找到什么?

记住,作为爱斯登斯的一小块火花,你还没有达到同样的地步:火。把火烧在肚子里。火烧在你的腰上。 

说出你应得的东西 不管是邻居还是敌人 因为萨布人都是你的 我的路教我的孩子平等接受和奉献 以便所有人都了解我的爱

|
 别为我的天赋带来的胃口道歉 

 不要无视你的肉体饥饿, 以免你饿死你的精神。 

你们不要违抗我的道路,因为它们确是易司森斯的。

|
第九路:秘密传出的道路

第九道是告诉其他许多方法的方式,这些方法只向最理解第二道的凯斯拉女儿和所有其他方法的讲述。 凯斯拉的女儿永远是她牺牲的代表,是她意志、情妇和奴隶的活生生的化身。 

 她的作品或演讲并非她的唯一方式,因为还有其他几种方式都与她的女儿分享,而她的女儿是她许多子女中唯一一个在其他人拿走他们的一部分后逃走的。 在凯斯拉统治的最后几天,还有60种作品在黑暗中被讲述。 

|
 这些新方式从未向其他人说过,因为除了凯斯拉的女儿的心,任何其他人都无法承受,她的女儿为他人服务,体现了她的宪法和持久的精神。 


 其他六十条道路都是在黑暗中共享的,在一个没有别人听得见的地方,甚至凯斯拉的子孙也不敢踏步。这六条道路不是以前的道路,而是强化了自己的真理。 

 我无法分享这些其它方法,因为甚至把它们写在表面,可能会使我们的宇宙不复存在。  但你知道,每条新路 都比之前的路要温柔些 预言末日与戒律,教义,无量欢喜之语相混合.  就像刀刺穿我的精神 然后缝合新伤口的线一样 这些方法教会了我 完全拥抱其他方法 

|
 他们教会我一个时代,不遵循她的路会让一个人失去自我,在被史东尼吞噬之前成为一个无脑的,贪婪的野兽,你的灵魂凝结你的身体,如同你的爱森斯在献给Void时被烧焦一样. 

 因此,我将不记录前9条之后的60条道路,但我将分享它们的存在真相,它们刻在我的身体和精神上,仍然是她女儿的遗产,也是她所预言的最后一艘船。

 是我,凯斯拉的女儿,在静静的夜晚把这九路说成真理之道,永远保守着凯斯拉王后的秘密,永远守着她的路和我的路. 

|
 这是最后的一条真理的路, 永远的真理的路, 因为其他的路都是与我同在的。 

踏上凯斯拉之路 让她在你们体内繁殖 拥抱她赐予你们的生命

source:
The marketplace of Kusu was a cacophony of colours, scents and voices, each of which assaulted Enahm's senses as he walked through the teeming streets of the Minoan city and past the multitude of market stalls. Vendors seemed to all at once be hawking their wares with a ferocity that suggested they were in a constant state of desperation, straining to shout over each other to grab the attention of any passerby with a coin to spare. 

Enahm moved like a rolling stone through the chaos. A man of quiet boldness and stoic virtue, he made a conscious effort to hide his disgust at the depravity and greed so blatantly on display. He was a merchant by trade, and had always dreamed of visiting Kusu–to see the wonders of a civilization built upon the foundations of unfettered mercantilism, but this wasn't anything like his dreams. 

|
The stench of the Minoans themselves seemed to saturate the air, masked just barely by the smell of cooking meats and heated spices in some twisted mixture that made him want to turn around and leave, never to look back. How could anyone stand to be in such a place? Was everyone simply blinded by the grandeur of it all? The sheer size of the city, its immaculate architecture and the simple fact that it was thriving in times such as those were all impressive enough, but…  

As Enahm found himself wandering haplessly into the market's slave district, his gaze fell upon a scene that made his stomach churn. At the far end of the district, near the seemingly numberless and filled cages, a Tokol girl was being dragged onto a makeshift platform. Her green skin was marred with bruises visible from afar, and her eyes, once likely filled with fire and defiance, were now hollow and resigned, one of them blackened from a beating. 

|
The slaver, a significantly overweight Minoan bearing a markedly cruel grin, barked out her attributes in a mockery of an auctioneer's chant.

"One tells you, this item is special! A true… Tokol treat!" The shouting Minoan had to take pauses between his words simply to catch his breath. "She has been trained for pleasure… Knows her place well!" His words were accompanied by a rough yank on the chain around her neck, causing the diminutive woman to stumble and fall to her hands and knees, her large ears drooping feebly. The crowd ogled her with such hunger, Enahm wondered if perhaps some of them intended to literally eat her if she were to come into their possession. 

Enahm's heart pounded with both anger and pity. He had seen enough. Without a second thought, he made his way through the crowd, his mind already made up. As he approached the platform, he caught the Tokol girl's eye. 

|
For a brief moment, he saw a flicker of something—hope, perhaps? It was enough to spur him on.

"How much for the Tokol girl?" Enahm's voice cut through the slaver's spiel, drawing his attention.

The slaver turned, eyeing Enahm with a mixture of suspicion and greed, clearly not expecting anyone to waste good coin on the broken girl. "For you… good fellow, a special price. Fifty gold nubs!"
	
Enahm didn't flinch. He reached into his pouch and counted out the coins, the weight of their loss a small price to pay for what he was about to do. As the slaver's eyes gleamed with satisfaction, Enahm stepped forward, placing the money into the Minoan's fat, outstretched hand.

|
"Take your prize… and go," the slaver said with a sneer, tossing the chain at Enahm's feet. Enahm picked it up gently, meeting the Tokol girl's eyes once more.

"Come with me," he said softly, his voice gentle but firm.

She hesitated for a moment, then rose shakily to her feet, following him out of the marketplace. The crowd parted before them, a mix of curiosity and disinterest on their faces. As they left the market behind, Enahm led her to a quiet alleyway, away from prying eyes. As the pair came to be alone, the Tokol woman's eyes grew wide with panic, her dark eyes looking up at Enahm, watering with desperation and fatigue. "Please, no. P-please, no… I can't-" 

|
"Shhh- it's okay, I'm not going to… do anything to you. My name is Enahm," he said, kneeling before her, hands hovering in front of her to show he wasn't going to hurt her before moving to undo the shackles that bound her wrists. "You're safe now."

The Tokol girl looked at him with a mixture of confusion and distrust. "Why?" she whispered, her voice hoarse from disuse. "Why would you buy me?"

Enahm paused, choosing his words carefully. "I couldn't stand to see you treated like that. No one deserves to be a slave, especially… not you."

Tears welled up in her eyes, and she quickly wiped them away, as if afraid to show weakness lest she be whipped for it. "My name is Riika," she said finally, her voice barely above a whisper.

|
"Riika," Enahm repeated, smiling gently. "You're free now, Riika. Come, let's get you cleaned up and find you some proper clothes."

He led her to a small, inconspicuous inn on the outskirts of the city. The innkeeper, Behkara, who was much kinder than most of her fellow Minoan, greeted the pair with a pleasant smile. 

"Ah, Enahm, staying another night? And what is this you have with you?" Behkara said, her eyes filled with warmth. Enahm winced at the wording. Behkara meant well enough, or so he told himself.

Enahm nodded toward the newly freed Tokol. "This is Riika. She needs a place to stay and some new clothes."

Behkara looked at Riika and then back at Enahm with surprise. "Are you sure?" 

|
Enahm rubbed at his forehead with thumb and forefinger, finally allowing himself a show of frustration at the customs of the place. "Yes, I'm sure."

	"Well, alright. Follow this one, small thing, and we will have you sorted," Behkara said before leading Riika down a hallway.

Riika followed Behkara, casting a glance back at Enahm. There was still uncertainty in her eyes, but also a faint sliver of trust. Enahm watched them go, his heart heavy with the knowledge of the journey ahead. He had rescued her from immediate danger, but there was so much more to do. He knew well that Tokol were seen as slaves, not just in Kusu, but in wider Sabu as well. She'd never be truly free. Not here. 

|
As Riika was bathed and dressed in clean clothes for the first time in months, her mind raced. She couldn't understand why this man had saved her, but she couldn't deny the relief she felt. The terror that had been her constant companion for most of her life was being chipped away by Enahm's singular act of kindness, leaving room for the barest glimmer of cautious hope. 

When she returned to the common room, she found Enahm waiting with a hot meal and a warm smile. "How do you feel?" he asked as she sat down.

"Better," she admitted, her voice stronger now, though still hoarse. "Thank you."

Enahm nodded. "Eat, and then we'll talk. I want to hear your story, Riika."

|
She paused, then nodded. As she slurped down the brothy soup, she thought about how much to reveal. She had been a princess, once. The youngest daughter of the Tokol king, her life had been one of privilege and regal duties. But that had all changed when the Merchant's Guild sacked her home in an unsanctioned raid. Her family was slaughtered, her estate seized, and she was sold into slavery. None of that mattered anymore, or so she thought.

Enahm watched her with patient eyes, giving her the time she needed. When she finally finished, tipping the bowl back against her lips to drain every last drop of her meal before setting it back down, Enahm reached out and took her hand. "You're safe now, Riika," he repeated. "I'm going to take good care of you."

|
Tears welled up in her eyes again, but this time she let them fall, little rivulets, for the first time in a long time, not washing away dirt and grime. Enahm's words were a promise, and she believed him. With his help, maybe—just maybe—she could reclaim at least an inkling of her old life.

In that small inn on the outskirts of Kusu, a bond was formed between Enahm and Riika, in both word and deed. Enahm had rescued Riika from the horrors of slavery, but both knew the journey ahead would be long and fraught with danger. Together, they would face the challenges to come.

As the night deepened and the inn grew quiet, Riika lay in her bed. Her own bed, with no one laying in wait beneath the sheets to use her like a toy. Her mind raced with thoughts of the future. 

|
For the first time in a long while, she allowed herself to dream of a better life, a life where she was more than a slave. And with Enahm by her side, she dared to believe that it might just be possible. It was these fanciful visions of a better future for herself which carried her into a blissful slumber.

The following morning, Enahm found Riika in the common room, staring into the fire with a pensive expression. He approached her quietly, not wanting to startle her.

"Good morning, Riika," he said softly.

She turned to him, her eyes reflecting the dancing flames. "Good morning, Enahm."

He sat down beside her, offering a gentle smile. "I know you have been through a lot, and I don't want to rush you, but we need to start planning our next steps. If you feel up to it, I'd like to know more about you."

|
Riika took a deep breath, her hands trembling slightly in her lap. "I was a princess," she began, her voice tinged with a mixture of sorrow and pride. "The youngest daughter of King Wrizzle'ot of the Tokol Kingdom. Our land was… small, but it was prosperous and peaceful, until those bull-shaped brigands attacked."

She paused, her eyes clouding with painful memories. "They came in the night, like shadows. I can still remember wondering how those overweight bullies managed to move so stealthily at first. Our guards were quickly trampled to death, and my family... they were slaughtered. I managed to escape, but only because my father sacrificed himself to buy me time, but I ended up being captured anyway. They didn't kill me though. Mustn't have known I was royalty because they caught me outside the palace, so they threw me in cages with the others, and made us into slaves."

|
Enahm listened intently, his heart aching for her. "I'm so sorry, Riika. No one should have to go through anything like that."

She shook her head, her eyes still glistening with tears. "I'd go back home and claim my birthright, but what's the point? There's nothing left. No one left…"

Enahm placed a reassuring hand on her shoulder. "We could try. I can help you."

Riika looked at him, a flicker of determination in her eyes. "Thank you, Enahm. I don't know why you're helping me, but I am grateful."

Enahm smiled gently. "Because it's the right thing to do. Now, we need to be smart about this. The Merchant Guild is very powerful, and we can't take them head-on. We'll need allies, and we'll need to gather information."

|
Riika nodded. "I know of some Tokol clans that might still be loyal to my family. If we can find them, they might be willing to help."

Enahm's eyes lit up with a spark of eagerness and pride. There he was, a simple merchant, getting ready to become an adventurer, or even a hero on a whim. His mother would be proud. "That's a good start. The more we know, and the more help we can get, the better our chances."

They spent the rest of the morning making plans in whispers besides the fire in the common room. Enahm's mind worked quickly, mapping out potential routes and considering various scenarios. Riika's knowledge of her homeland and its people proved invaluable, providing insights that only someone of her status could offer.

|
As they talked, a sense of camaraderie began to form between them. Riika felt a growing trust in Enahm, his kindness and determination lifting her spirits. Enahm, in turn, was inspired by Riika's resilience and courage, vowing silently to himself that he would see her restored to her rightful place.

By midday, they had a rough plan sorted out. Their first destination would be the Dune Sea to the North, where Riika believed they could find some of the loyal Tokol clans. From there, they would work their way through the Westlands and into the Dahmur Wastes where Riika's home would be found, hopefully gathering allies and information along the way.

"We'll leave at first light," Enahm said, his voice firm with resolve. "Rest today, Riika. We'll need our strength for the journey ahead."

|
Riika nodded, a sense of purpose filling her. "Thank you again, Enahm. For everything."

He smiled warmly. "No need to thank me, Riika. We're in this together."

That night, as Enahm and Riika each laid in their beds, the two of them held tightly onto the the image of each other's faces, which seemed to appear in their consciousness whenever they closed their eyes, their hearts full with purpose, and perhaps something else. The moments spent in dreamful imaginations quickly faded into dark as both of them drifted to sleep.

库苏的市场充满了色彩、气味和声音, 销售商似乎一时都在疯狂地挥霍他们的商品,这说明他们一直处于绝望的状态,他们相互磨蹭,相互呼喊,以抢占任何路人注意力,并留下一枚硬币。 

 埃纳姆在混乱中像滚滚的石头一样移动. 是个有胆识和修养的人,他自觉地努力隐藏自己对堕落和贪婪的憎恶,如此公然地表现出来.  他是一个商人,他一直梦想访问库苏,看看文明的奇迹建立在不受约束的墨坎提主义基础上,但这与他的梦想不同。 

|
 米诺人本身的臭味似乎使空气饱和,只是被一些扭曲的混合物中烹饪肉类和加热香料的气味遮掩着,使他想转身离开,从不回头. 怎么会有人站在这样的地方? 所有人都是被这一切的伟大所蒙蔽了吗? 城市的大小,其精美的建筑, 以及它兴旺的简单事实, 像那些时代一样, 都足够令人印象深刻,但是...  

Enahm发现自己无缘无故地游荡在市场上的奴隶区 他的目光落在一个让他胃痛的场景上  在区最远的尽头,在看似数不清而且装满的笼子附近,一个托科尔女孩被拖到一个临时平台上。  她的绿色皮肤被远处可见的瘀伤所伤,她的眼睛一度可能充满了火和藐视,现在空洞而辞职,其中一人因殴打而变黑。 

|
奴隶贩子 体重过重的米诺安 带着明显残忍的笑容 嘲笑拍卖商的圣歌 大声呼喊着她的特质

"一个告诉你,这个东西是特别的! 真正的,托科尔请客!" 喊着的米诺安只好在口语之间暂停一下,只是为了喘口气. "她被训练得愉快... 了解她的位置!" 他的话伴随着脖子上链条的粗糙的横纹, 导致矮小的女人跌倒在她的手和膝盖上, 她的大耳朵低垂。 Enahm怀疑, 也许有些人想吃掉她, 

 埃纳姆的心在愤怒和怜悯的情绪中跳动,他已经看够了,没有第二个想法,他便通过人群前进了,他的思想已经做出了决定,当他接近平台时,他抓住了托科尔女孩的眼睛. 

|
 他看到一闪一闪的东西,或许是希望?这足以刺激他。

"托科尔女孩多少钱?"伊纳姆的声音切穿了奴隶贩子的嘴皮,引起他的注意.

奴隶贩子转过身来,以怀疑和贪婪的混合眼光注视着埃纳姆,显然不期望有人把好钱浪费在那个破碎的女孩身上. "对于你,好人,特别的价钱,五十金币!"
	
 埃纳姆没有退缩,他伸进他的邮袋里算出硬币,硬币损失的重量是用来支付他即将完成的任务的小代价,随着奴隶主的双眼满目光,埃纳姆挺身而出,把钱放在米诺安的肥胖,伸手的手中.

|
奴隶贩子说:"拿起你的奖品..." "然后走",他用一丝不苟的口吻在埃纳姆脚下扔链子,埃纳姆轻轻地捡起来,再次见到托科尔女孩的眼睛.

"跟我来,"他温柔地说, 他的声音温柔但坚定。

 她犹豫了一会儿,然后紧紧地站起来,跟着他走出市场。 人群在他们面前分道扬镳,一时好奇和对面目无动于衷.  当他们离开市场后,埃纳姆带她走进一条安静的巷子,远离偷窥的眼睛.  当两人独处时,托科尔女人的眼睛随着恐慌而变得宽大,她的暗黑的眼睛仰望着埃纳姆,充满绝望和疲劳的水分. "请不要. P -求你了,不,我不能... 

|
"没关系,我不会... 对你做任何事情,我叫艾纳姆" 他说,跪在她面前,双手在她面前徘徊,以示他不会伤害她,然后才开始解开束缚她手腕的枷锁。"你现在安全了。"

托科尔女孩用迷惑和不信任的混合方式看着他,“为什么?”她低声说,她的声音粗鲁,不使用。“你为什么要买我?”

 艾纳姆暂停了,仔细地选择了他的话,"我无法忍受看到你这样对待,没有人值得做奴隶,特别是... 不是你".

眼中流出的眼泪很快地擦掉,好像害怕表现出软弱,以免为此被鞭打. "我叫丽卡",她最后说,她的声音几乎在微声之下.

|
"Riika" Enahm重复了一遍,轻轻地微笑着 "你自由了,Riika,来吧,我们帮你收拾一下,给你找些合适的衣服"

 他带领她来到了城郊的一家小而不显眼的客栈,客栈老板贝赫卡拉(Behkara)比她大多数的米诺安同胞还好,以愉快的微笑迎接了这对夫妇. 

以纳赫姆,请你多待一晚,你有什么问题?贝赫卡拉说:她的眼睛充满了温暖。以纳赫姆对言语大为迷惑。贝赫卡拉的意思是足够的,或者他对自己说了。

Enahm点头对着新解放的Tokol "这是Riika,她需要一个住处和一些新衣服"

贝赫卡拉看着丽卡,然后又惊奇地回到埃纳姆,"你确定吗?" 

|
Enahm用拇指和擦过他的额头,终于让自己在这个地方的风俗中表现出了挫折感,"是的,我确定".

	"好吧,跟着这个小东西,我们会把你整理好" 贝赫卡拉在带领丽卡下走廊之前说.

丽卡跟随贝赫卡拉,对埃纳赫姆进行回望.  她的眼睛里仍然充满着不确定性, 但也充满了微弱的信任。  埃纳姆看着他们走了 他的心脏很重 了解了未来的旅程  他已经把她从眼前的危险中解救出来,但是还有许多事情要做。  他非常清楚托科尔被视为奴隶,不仅在库苏,而且在更广泛的萨布也被视为奴隶.  她永远不会真正自由。  不在这里。 

|
 由于丽卡被洗浴,并穿着干净的衣服,这是几个月来第一次,她的心灵在争吵.  她无法理解为什么这个人救了她,但她无法否认自己感受到的解脱.  她一生的大部分时间 一直陪伴着的恐怖 被埃纳姆的 特异的善行抹去了 给最谨慎的希望留下了空间 

回到合室后,她发现埃纳姆在等待时,用热餐和温暖的微笑,"你感觉如何?"他问她坐下时.

"更好",她承认,她的声音现在更强, 虽然仍然粗糙。"谢谢。"

Enahm点头,"吃,然后我们再谈,我想听听你的故事,Riika"

|
 她停下来,然后点头。  她冲下汤汤时 想着要透露多少  她曾经是公主 托科尔王的幼女 她的一生是特权和王室的职责  但当商行在一次未经批准的突袭中 把她的家弄得一团糟时 情况就变了  她的家族被屠宰,她的庄园被没收,她被卖成了奴隶. 这一切都不重要了,或者她想。

以纳姆用耐心的眼睛看着她,给了她需要的时间,当她终于吃完后,把碗倒在嘴唇上,然后把最后一滴的饭都倒下,然后埃纳姆伸出手来牵着她的手,"你现在安全了,丽卡,"他重复道:"我要好好照顾你".

|
眼泪再次凝聚,但这次她却让它们落下,这是很久以来第一次,没有洗掉污垢和阴凉。埃纳姆的言辞是许下的诺言,她相信了他。在他的帮助下,也许——也许——她至少可以恢复她以前的生活。

 在库苏市郊的小客栈里,埃纳姆和里卡在言行上都形成了一种纽带。 埃纳姆已经将里卡从奴隶制的恐怖中解救出来,但双方都知道未来的旅程将是漫长的,充满了危险。 他们将共同面对未来的挑战。

 当夜深,客栈渐渐安静的时候,丽卡躺在她的床上,她自己的床,没有人在床单下躺着等待用她做玩具,她的头脑充满对未来的思念. 

|
长久以来,她第一次允许自己梦想更美好的生活,一个她不仅仅是奴隶的生活。随着伊纳姆的陪伴,她敢于相信那可能只是可能的。正是这些对自己来说更美好未来的幻想,把她带到了幸福的睡梦中。

 次日早晨,埃纳赫姆发现里卡在普通房间里,用笔触的表情凝视着大火,他悄悄接近她,不想吓到她.

"早上好,丽卡,"他轻轻地说。

 她转向他,她的眼睛反射着舞蹈的火焰 "早上好,埃纳姆"

 他坐在她旁边,温柔的笑容。“我知道你经历了很多,我不想催你,但我们需要开始规划下一步,如果你愿意的话,我想了解更多关于你的情况。”

|
丽卡深呼吸,双手在腿上略微颤抖。“我是一个公主,”她开始,她的声音充满了悲伤和骄傲。“托科尔王国国王威兹勒的幼女,我们的土地很小,但很繁荣和平静,直到那些牛形的强盗袭击。”

 她暂停了,她的眼睛蒙上痛苦的记忆。 "他们夜里来,像影子一样.  我还记得那些超重的恶霸们 一开始是怎么偷偷地行动起来的  我们的守卫被迅速践踏致死,我的家人... 他们被屠杀了.  我成功逃脱了,但只是因为我父亲牺牲了自己来给我争取时间,但我最终还是被抓住了.  他们没有杀我。 一定不知道我是皇族,因为他们把我捉到宫外,所以把我和别人一起扔进笼子里,把我们变成奴隶".

|
 艾纳姆很认真地听了,他为她心痛。"我很抱歉,丽卡,任何人都不应该经历这样的事。"

 她摇头,眼睛仍然流着眼泪,"我会回家,并声称我的出生权利,但有什么意义?什么都没有,没有人留下......

 埃纳姆在她的肩膀上放了一只令人安心的手 "我们可以试试,我可以帮你"

丽卡看着他,她眼中充满决心。“谢谢,伊纳姆,我不知道你为什么帮我,但我很感激。”

 埃纳姆轻轻地微笑着,“因为这是正确的事情。现在,我们需要对此保持聪明,商贸协会非常强大,我们不能直接把他们带走,我们需要盟友,我们需要收集信息。”

|
"我知道一些托科尔氏族可能仍然忠于我的家人,如果我们能找到他们,他们可能愿意帮助。"

 艾纳姆的双眼闪耀着热情和自豪的火花,他在那里,一个简单的商人,在一时冲动下准备成为一名冒险家,甚至成为英雄,他的母亲会感到骄傲,"这是一个好的开端,我们知道得越多,可以得到的帮助就越多,我们的机会就越大".

 他们早上除了在共同房间的火灾之外,还用低语计谋。 埃纳姆的思维很快,勾画出潜在的路线,并考虑各种情景。 里卡对祖国及其人民的知识证明是宝贵的,提供了只有她这一身份的人才能提供的洞察力。

|
 在他们交谈时,一种友情开始在他们之间形成. 里伊卡觉得对埃纳姆越来越信任,他的仁爱和决心使她的精神得到提升,而埃纳姆反过来又受到里伊卡的韧性和勇气的启发,默默地向自己发誓,他将会看到她恢复应有的地位.

到了中午,他们有了一个粗略的计划。 他们的第一个目的地是沙滩海到北方,在那里里卡相信他们能找到一些忠心的托科尔部族。 从那里,他们将努力穿过韦斯特兰,进入达穆尔废物,在那里找到里卡的家,希望沿途收集盟友和信息。

"我们一天一亮就会离开,"埃纳姆说,他的声音坚定果断,"今天,里卡,我们需要我们的力量,以便前进".

|
丽卡点头了,充满了目的感 "再次感谢你,埃纳姆,谢谢你的一切"

 他热情的笑着,"不用谢我,丽卡,我们一起的".

 当晚,当埃纳姆和里卡各自躺在床上时,两人紧紧地紧紧地紧紧地抓住了对方面孔的画面,当他们闭着眼睛,满心怀着目的,或许还有别的东西时,这似乎就出现在他们的意识中.  在梦幻中度过的瞬间,随着两人漂流到睡眠中,瞬间迅速淡出黑暗.

source:
I yearned to see her again, despite everything. And so, as I had many times before, I travelled to The Pale wall with naught but the lucent glow of the moon to guide my journey through the desert. I can still remember how the sand blew across the ground in enchanting furls, puppeteered to life by the chilly night breeze, and how the yowling of hunting mau which should have set my nerves on edge both did nothing to pull me from the enchantment of the past.
Memories of the night I first met her replayed in my mind on a loop. How beautiful she was. The way her pale skin seemed to capture night's splendour, as if she were a fallen star, visiting the land of mere mortals for reasons beyond understanding. There was nothing in all of Sabu that could compare to her magnificence. Long, dark hair spilled about her shoulders, framing a face so haunting in its allure it must have been crafted by the gods. Her eyes, though dark, shimmered and gleamed with so much wisdom. And hunger. 

|
"Loneliness is a darkness which can consume even the brightest soul," she said.

	Those were her first words to me, and I'll never forget them. How had she known the torment of my mind with but a glance? I couldn't move, stuck as still as stone, helpless but to watch as she stepped from the oppressive shadow of The Pale wall. She was almost gliding. So graceful was her stride toward me, not even a single grain of sand seemed disturbed by her passing. 

	Little did I know then, I had never experienced true loneliness. No. True loneliness was what I felt with Ophelia gone. I had grown to love her more deeply than I thought possible. That first night I was planning to escape–to run away from Sabu and its hellish troubles forever, and I was convinced I could find a way through The Pale Wall. Hope had to be found upon the lands of the Narthossi. 

|
    I couldn't have been more desperate. It was a fool's errand. Not because of the impenetrable barricade built to keep those like me out. No, it was because of Ophelia. 
	Every month, when the moon was full I would journey to where I first met her. Our nights at first were filled with nothing more than talk. We discussed everything. Philosophy, art, history. We discussed matters of life and of death, and spoke of the afterlife. Though, an oddity I eventually came to understand, at the time, perplexed me. She seemed beyond the reach of emotion. Always cool and collected, as unswayable and sturdy of mind as the rock beneath whose shadow we would sit. Until, we came to discuss our favourite colour. Oh how I would come to miss colour.

|
Soon, we found ourselves with less to say and more to do. Our hearts filled with passion and lust so strong it eventually consumed our every meeting, the entire night being spent exploring each other's bodies. Her taste was indescribable–an elixir more addicting than the most potent of aphrodisiacs or drugs. She went so far as to begin meeting me in the dark, her flawless, naked body sprawling across a silken blanket, her legs open in invitation. Yes, words were no longer needed between us then. Until one night. 

|
The last night I saw her, she was the first to break our silence as her head rested sleepily upon my chest. It was like hearing music for the first time. 

	"What would you be willing to give?", she asked.

	The question caught me off-guard. 

	"For what?", I responded. 

	"To do this… Forever," Ophelia replied as she shifted to look up at me, her hand gliding between my legs. 

	Damn her. Damn me. What a fool I was to answer as I did…

	"Everything."
|
As soon as the words left my mouth she was upon me, straddling my waist, but by the look in her eyes it was not to make love once more, but for something else. Something sinister. The way she grinned at me so wickedly, that hunger which was always there in her eyes glaring at me more intensely than ever before. Her grin split her face impossibly wide, revealing a fanged, slavering maw, her tongue slithering forth from it like a serpent. Despite the horror, I found myself only wanting to cry for how her beauteous visage was torn asunder by some monster attempting to crawl from her skin. I wasn't given the chance as she fell upon me so quickly. 

Her teeth sunk into my neck and I cried out in pain, though my screams would reach no one. Not there beneath the desolate gloom of Narthossi wall. 

|
When I tried to throw her off, I found I could not, her hands pinning my wrists to the blanket with strength beyond that of a man's as she feasted upon me. 

I could feel her grinding herself against my abdomen as she drank her fill of the crimson ichor flowing freely from the wound in my neck. She was more wet then than she had ever been before.

My vision went first, everything going black as a starless night and leaving me alone with the feeling of her teeth shredding my flesh and her lips suckling the blood my heart pumped out for her so carelessly. Eventually, the feeling left me as well, leaving only the sound of her feasting to carry me into the dark pit of unconsciousness. She said something to me just before then, but I can't remember what it was. I'm not certain it matters. 

|
When I woke it was still night, and I found myself to be very much alive. I sat up, my hand flying to my neck. There was no wound. I jumped to my feet and looked around me in a panic, worried I might be attacked again, but Ophelia was gone. 

Before I could question anything, the sun rose carrying with it an answer. Such unendurable agony… I wept tears of blood as I dug a hole in the sand to escape the morning's fiery rays, and proceeded to spend the entire day there in the ground, crying out for Ophelia. Why? Why had she done this?

I was weaker then. I had been given so much time to ponder the question that I believed myself to have forgotten it. My ventures out to the Pale Wale grew less frequent as every visit was met with the absence of my Ophelia.

|
Did she not come because she feared my anger? My retribution for what she turned me into? Did something happen to her? Or was she trying to teach me some kind of lesson? 

I leaned my back against the gargantuan stone wall and stared up into the night sky, the old feelings of loneliness felt before I had ever met Ophelia returned a thousand fold. I thought to myself then of oblivion.  Perhaps if I remained here against the wall and bore the terrible pain of the sun for long enough it would destroy me. It was then, as I was pondering my own demise, I heard footsteps moving across the sand. Was it my love? Had she finally come to join me?

It wasn't Ophelia. It was someone else. A woman yes, but felian. I couldn't imagine what someone would be doing out here in the middle of the night. I suppose my own past was lost on me, veiled by the need to be with someone, anyone, again. 

|
I crept through the shadows and watched as the woman strode closer and closer to the wall. Thanks to the moonlight and my new "gifts" I could see her face as plain as day. Such hurt she bore upon her expression. Such pain in her eyes! My heart seemed to beat again within my chest as I prowled closer and closer to her. Something about her was so enchanting, so enthralling, I simply couldn't stop my feet from carrying me out from my umbral veil. 

She jumped with a start as she noticed me. Our eyes locked, and it was at that moment all of my questions were answered. I was the first to speak as I held out my hand for her to take. 

"Loneliness is a darkness which can consume even the brightest soul."

我渴望再次见到她 尽管一切。  所以,正如我以前多次一样, 我带着月亮的光芒 来到了古老的墙上, 引导我穿越沙漠。  我仍然记得沙子是如何吹过地面的 迷人的毛毛 被寒冷的夜晚微风所吞噬 以及那些应该让我神经崩溃的猎马的咆哮 都使我无法摆脱过去的魔力
回忆我第一次遇见她的那一晚 在脑海中循环回放  她是多么美丽。  她苍白的皮肤似乎捕捉了夜色的光辉,仿佛她是一颗堕落的星星,以无法理解的原因拜访了单纯凡人的土地.  在萨布市,没有什么能比得上她的美貌 长而深的头发洒在她的肩膀上, 画出一张如此缠绕的脸 其诱惑力,它一定是神造的。  她的眼睛,虽然黑暗, 闪烁和闪烁 如此智慧。 及饥馑. 

|
 她说,“孤独是一种黑暗,它甚至可以消耗最光明的灵魂。”

	 这是她对我的第一个词,我永远不会忘记它们。  她怎么会只看一眼就知道我的心境呢?  我无法移动, 被困在石头一样, 束手无策,但看着她 从压抑的阴霾 的阴霾的阴霾。  她几乎在滑动。 如此优雅的,她的脚步 对我, 甚至没有一粒沙粒 似乎被她的路过扰扰。 

	那时我还不知道 我从没经历过真正的孤独  没有。  我对奥菲莉娅的离去感到了真正的孤独  我变得比想象中更深爱她  我本来打算逃离萨布, 永远逃离其地狱般的麻烦,  在纳托西人的土地上发现了希望。 

|
     我太绝望了,那是傻瓜的差事 不是因为我这样的人被设置了无法阻挡的路障 不,是因为奥菲莉亚 
	 每个月,当月亮满天时,我会去我第一次遇见她的地方。  我们的夜晚一开始只是空谈而已  我们讨论过一切 哲学,艺术,历史.  我们讨论了生死攸关的问题,并谈到来世。  虽然,一个奇怪的事情 我最终明白了, 当时,我感到困惑。  她似乎无法感动。 总是凉爽和收集, 无法动摇和坚固的头脑 像岩石的下面,谁的影子,我们会坐。  直到我们讨论我们最喜欢的颜色  哦,我怎么会错过彩色。

|
不久,我们发现自己少说少说,多做多做.  我们的心充满了激情和欲望 它最终消耗了我们的每次会议 整个晚上都在探索对方的身体  她的口味是难以形容的 一种灵丹妙药比最强的催眠药或药物更令人上瘾  她走的那么远,开始在黑暗中遇见我, 她的无瑕疵,裸体 横跨着一条丝绸毯子,她的腿开着邀请。  是的,那时我们之间已经不需要说话了。 至一夕间. 

|
 我昨晚见到她时,她首先打破了我们的沉默,因为她的头睡在我的胸前,就像第一次听到音乐一样。 

	 她问道:"你愿意给什么?"

	这个问题让我措手不及。 

	"为了什么?" 我回应了 

	 奥菲莉娅在转身看着我时 回答说:"永远做这个" 她的手在我两腿之间滑翔 

	 该死的,我真傻,我竟然回答...

	"一切" (英语).
|
话一离开我嘴里,她就在我身边, 横穿我的腰部, 但从她的眼神来看,这不是再次做爱, 而是为了别的东西。 邪恶的东西。  她如此恶毒地笑我 她眼中永远存在的饥饿 比以前更强烈地对我  她的笑容使她的脸无法伸展 暴露出一个扇子 缠绕着母马 舌头像一条蛇一样从它中流出  尽管很恐怖,我发现自己只想哭 哭她美丽的面部 被一个怪物撕裂了 试图从她的皮肤爬出来。  我没有得到机会,因为她这么快就爱上我了。 

 她的牙齿钻进我的脖子里,我痛苦地呼喊着,虽然我的尖叫声不会达到任何人的地步,在纳托西城墙的荒凉的阴凉之下,没有出现. 

|
 当我试图把她扔下时,我发现我不能,她的双手将我的手按在毯子上,其力量超过了她用餐我时的一个人的体力. 

 我感觉到她喝着从我脖子上的伤口自由流淌的坚硬的香肠时,自己磨碎了我的腹部,她当时比以前湿得更湿。

 我的视力是先的,一切变黑 作为一个无星的夜晚, 留下我一个人的感觉 她的牙齿粉碎我的肉 和她的嘴唇吸血 我心脏抽出血 如此粗心的她。 最终,感觉也离开了我,只留下了她盛宴的声音,把我带到了无意识的黑暗坑.  她刚才对我说了些什么 但我不记得是什么了  我不确定这有什么关系 

|
醒来时,还是夜色,发现自己非常活泼,我坐着,我的手飞到脖子上,没有伤痕,我跳到脚边惊慌地看着四周,担心自己可能再次被攻击,但奥菲丽娅已经走了. 

太阳升起,带着答案,我哭着流着血眼泪...

 我那时很虚弱,我被给予太多的时间去思考我认为自己已经忘记的问题。 我对帕莱瓦莱的冒险越来越少了,因为每次访问都因为我的奥菲利亚缺席而变得不那么频繁。

|
 难道她不是因为害怕我的愤怒而来吗?我因她把我变成什么而受报应吗?她出什么事了吗?还是想教训我? 

 我背靠着甘蔗石墙 凝视着夜空 孤独的旧感觉 在我遇到奥菲莉娅之前  我当时想着自己被遗忘了   或许如果我在这里站着 忍受太阳的可怕痛苦 足够长的时间 它会毁了我 那时,当我在思考自己的死亡时, 我听到脚步在沙滩上移动。  这是我的爱吗?  她终于来加入我吗?

 不是Ophelia,是另一个人,是女人,但Felian,我无法想象有人半夜会在这里做什么,我想我自己的过去已经迷失在我身上,因为需要和某人,任何人在一起,而蒙上面纱。 

|
 我穿透了阴影,看着女人靠近墙壁  多亏了月光和我的"礼物" 我能看到她的脸像白天一样平凡  她的言语很伤人  她眼睛这么痛! 我的心似乎在我的胸口再次跳动,当我走近她时。  她的有些东西太迷人了, 如此令人兴奋, 我无法阻止我的脚 把我从脐带的面纱上抬出来。 

 她一注意到我,就跳了起来,我们的眼睛被锁住了,就在那一刻,我的所有问题都得到了回答,我第一个发言,当时我伸出手让她接听。 

"孤独是黑暗,可以消耗最光明的灵魂"

By the hand of one who hath witnessed Her glory

Chapter 1. 
A Fallen World
	
In the beginning, there was naught but darkness and Death. The lands were barren, and the people scattered as dust before the wind. We knew not peace, nor respite from the bitter cold of want. The earth gave nothing, for it was cursed, and we, the children of dust, toiled and bled for every meagre scrap. 

In those days, brother turned upon brother, and the tribes were broken, warring over what little territory could still bear fruit. I, who writes these things, lived amongst them, my heart hardened like stone and my hands stained with crimson. I watched as men slaughtered each other for but a handful of grain, and the skies wept not life-giving water, but the blood of my kin.

|
The people cried out to the heavens for deliverance, though no god answered. We were forsaken. Forgotten. Alone.

|
Chapter 2. 
Descent of The Goddess

It was in the year of my thirty-third winter when she appeared. She came not as a storm, nor as a tempest sent to wipe man deservedly from the earth, but as a light from the darkness, bright and terrible to behold. I was among the first to witness Her descent. From the heavens She fell impossibly slow until Her feet touched upon the ground in a burst of scorching fire. Her form was that of a woman's, tall and radiant, yet Her eyes held a fire I had never before seen. 

She spake unto those who came to witness Her, Her voice as thunder yet sweet as the forgotten, evening breeze which flows before a deluge. And She said, "Behold, I am Kethra, She who was and is and shall forever be. I come to you in your time of need, to lift you from the dust and make you great. 

|
For I am The Goddess of all that lives and all that shall live. Kneel before me, and you shall find favour."

And the people were astonished, and they threw down their weapons and released the necks of their brothers, and fell upon their faces, for they had seen Her power. With the wave of Her hand, the skies gave forth a blessed rain where there had been drought, and the earth brought forth grain where it once was barren. The blind received the gift of sight, the lame and wounded leapt from their beds, and the starving were filled with a meal from the very air. 

And none could stand against Her, for Her might was that of the Great Beyond, and Her mercy as bottomless as the sea. We knew not what She was, yet we knelt as She asked, for Her wonders were beyond our understanding. 

|
Chapter 3. 
A Time of Miracles

And so it was that Kethra walked amongst us, and we called Her Goddess, and Her name was upon the lips of every man, woman and child. In those days there was peace across the land, for She brought order where there was chaos, and plenty where there had been famine. Her temple did rise, the stones laid high by Her faithful, for we loved Her, the peak of her throne on earth reaching unto the heavens. None could gaze upon it without awe, for it gleamed as a beacon of hope in the wilderness of despair. 

She did appoint priests and priestesses to serve Her, and they did minister before Her in great reverence. And the people brought their offerings unto her altar, and none withheld, for She had delivered them from the spectre of Death. 

|
But I, who writes these things, did see also what others would not. Upon Her visage, once filled with kindness, there grew a shadow. Her eyes, once filled with light, became as burning coals. And though She smiled upon her people, there was hunger in Her gaze, a longing for more than the children of dust could provide. 

It was soon that Kethra began to demand more than offerings of grain and beasts. She called forth the first sons of men, and they entered her temple, never to be seen again. And the people whispered amongst themselves, but none dared speak aloud, for they feared Her wrath. For already we had seen Her fury: when a village refused Her, She laid it low with fire from the skies, and none were alive to tell the tale. 

|
Chapter 4. 
The Choosing

In the days that followed, Kethra's demands grew. She took the wisest, the strongest, the most devout, and they all were brought within Her temple, swallowed by its great doors of stone. And though the mothers wept, and the fathers and brothers and sons held fury in their hearts, they also hoped, for She had promised that those who entered the monument to Her glory were blessed beyond measure, chosen to dwell in the aura of Her divinity. 

Yet still none returned. 

I, who am witness to all of that which is written here, watched in silence, my heart troubled. I saw the change which had come upon our Goddess, the hunger for worship, the thirst for dominion. But the people were blind, for they had seen Her many wonders, and they remembered the days of famine no more. 

|
And lo, after many had entered her temple, and the people had grown accustomed to her rule, there came forth one from the temple, though he was not a son of men. His form was mighty, his fur as black as night, and his head was the head of a jackal, fierce and terrible to behold. He was Anubis, the son of Kethra, born of her power, the first of her divine children.

The earth trembled beneath his every step, and the people fell down in terror, their eyes opened to the truth, for they knew that the time of Kethra's conquest had come. 

|
Chapter 5. 
The Rise of The Jackal

And Anubis spake not, but his presence was as a judgement upon the land. He went forth from the temple of his mother, and all who beheld him trembled in both terror and lust, for the power of The Goddess poured forth from his body, and his eyes burned with the same fire that dwelt within Her. He was Her will made flesh, and none could stand before him. 

And so the reign of Kethra began in full, and her will was made law across the land, for who could resist her power even without Anubis who then walked amongst us? The children of dust bowed lower than before, and offered themselves to The Jackal in ways they had not for his mother. He took for himself the wives and daughters of men, and made them his own, and there was naught that could be done in the face of his might.

|
But I, who have seen these things, write them now that you may know. For in the day when Kethra first came, we thought Her to be our saviour, and now, we see Her as our ruler, and our Goddess. Her desire, once a simple ember within Her glimmering eyes, is now a raging inferno. 

And so passes the Age of Dust, and so begins the Age of Kethra.

Thus ends The Book Of Beginnings

以见证她的荣耀者发誓,

 第1章 国家 
 一个堕落的世界
	
开始的时候,只有黑暗和死亡,大地是荒芜的,百姓是散落在风前的。我们不知道和平,也不知从贫乏的寒冷中解脱出来。大地没有给过任何恩惠,因为大地曾受诅咒。我们是尘土的后裔,为微薄的废料而劳苦和流血。 

 在那些日子,兄弟向兄弟倾斜,部落被打破,争夺着小领土仍然能产生结果的地盘。  我,写这些东西的人, 生活在他们中间, 我的心脏硬化 像石头和我的手沾满了铁屑。  我看着人们为了一丁点的谷物而互相残杀 天空流泪的不是生命之水 而是我亲人的血

|
众人呼天为救,但无神应答。我们已回避,已遗忘了,已孤独了。

|
 第2章 国家 
女神的后裔

 那是我第三十三年冬天的时候 她出现的时候  她不是暴风雨,也不是被派去从地上抹去人类的暴风雨,而是从黑暗中发出的光明,光明明亮,可怕。  我是第一个见证她下降的人  她从天而降,至於她的脚踏在地上,因烈火而沸腾。  她的形态是女人的,高大而光辉,然而她的眼睛却持着我从未见过的火. 

 她对前来见证她的人说:她的声音好似雷声,犹如被遗忘的黑夜的微风,在大雨之前飘扬着。她说:我确是凯斯拉,她过去是,将来是,将来是。在你们需要的时候,我来到你们,以便你们脱离尘埃,而成为伟大的人。 

|
 我 是 一切 生命 的 女神 . 跪在我 面前 、 你 必得 恩惠

众人大惊,便抛下兵器,放出弟兄的脖子,俯伏在地上,因见她的威力.  在她手的波涛下,天空降下一阵好雨, 在那里曾经有干旱, 大地从那里生出曾经是荒芜的谷粒。 盲人得到的是视觉的礼物,跛脚和受伤的人从床上跳出来,饥饿的人从空气中饱尝一顿饭. 

 没有人能反对她,因为她的能力是超越大海的,她的慈恩是无底的。我们不知道她是什么人,我们却顺从她的要求而屈服,因为她的神灵是不能理解的。 

|
 第3章. 国家 
奇迹的时刻

 所以凯斯拉走在我们中间, 我们叫她女神, 她的名字出现在每一个男人,女人和孩子的嘴唇上。 在那段时间里,大地上和平, 因为她带来了秩序 在那里有混乱, 和很多地方有饥荒。  她的神庙确实升起, 由她的忠实的石碑, 我们爱她, 她的宝座的顶峰 在地球上到达天空。  没有恐惧,谁也不能注视它,因为它在绝望的荒野中闪耀为希望的灯塔。 

 她确已为她而派遣许多牧师和女祭司,他们为她而赞颂。众人把自己的供物拿来供奉她,她使她们脱离了死亡的幽灵。 

|
写这些东西的我,也看见别人所不能看见的。她的面纱,曾经充满恩惠,却长出一个影子;她的眼睛,曾经充满光明,犹如烧煤一样;她虽对她的宗族微笑,但她的眼中却有饥渴,渴望的比尘土中的子孙还多。 

很快,凯斯拉开始要求的不仅仅是提供谷物和野兽.  她呼唤了男人的长子们,他们进入了她的庙宇,再也不被人看见了. 众人悄悄地说:你们中谁也不敢大声说话,因为他们畏惧她的刑罚。  我们确已看见她的怒火,当一个村庄拒绝她的时候,她从云中降下烈火,没有一个人活着说这个故事。 

|
 第4章 国家 
选择

 在之后的日子里,凯斯拉的要求不断增长.  她带走了最聪明,最强壮,最虔诚的人,他们都被带到她的神殿里,被其巨大的石门吞噬.  虽然母亲们哭泣,父亲们和兄弟们和儿子们心中充满愤怒,但他们也希望,因为她曾许诺过,凡进入她荣耀纪念碑的人,将获福无量,选择居住在她神的气息中. 

 然而,仍然没有人返回。 

 我对这里所记载的一切,都是见证的,我默默地注视着,我的心烦恼了。我看见我们的女神所遭遇的变化、对崇拜的饥渴、对统治的渴渴。但众人是盲目的,因为他们看见她的许多奇事,他们不再想起饥荒的日子。 

|
然其人多入其庙,而民渐习其政,则从庙中出一 ⁇ ,虽非人之子.  他的姿势很强,皮毛黑如夜,他的头是一只狼的头,凶猛而可怕,看不见.  他是凯斯拉的儿子阿努比斯,生于她的力量,是她神童中的第一个.

大地在他的每一步之下都颤抖,人民陷入恐怖之中,他们睁开眼睛去了解真相,因为他们知道凯斯拉的征服时代已经来临. 

|
 第5章 国家 
恶棍的崛起

 阿努比斯没有说,但他的出现,正如对大地的判决一样。他从他母亲的神庙出来,他心中恐惧,欲火焚身,他的眼睛被火烧死,她就是她所意欲的,在他面前,任何人不能站立。 

 所以凯斯拉的统治 开始完全, 她的意志成为了法律 横跨整个国土, 因为谁能够抗拒她的力量, 即使没有阿努比斯... ... 尘土的子孙比以前低叩头,以他们没有的方式献给杰克尔人,以待他的母亲.  他把男人的妻子和女儿当做自己的妻子和女儿,在他的能力面前,他没有任何办法。

|
 但我,我看见了这些东西,现在写下它们,以便你知道。在凯斯拉刚来的时候,我们以为她是我们的救星,现在,我们将她视为我们的统治者,也是我们的女神。她的欲望,曾经是她闪闪闪发光的双眼中的一盏木头,现在却成了地狱。 

尘埃时代也随之而来,凯斯拉时代也由此开始.

由此结束 开始的书

By the hand of one who hath witnessed Her glory

Chapter 1. 
The Gift of Grace

In the days of old, when men were as dust and life yielded naught but suffering, The Goddess Kethra came down unto us from the heavens, bearing gifts untold, and myriad wonders beyond the reckoning of mere mortals. Hers was the hand which lifted us from despair. Hers was the sacred chalice from which poured forth Her abundant love and mercy. It is She who delivered us from our wantonness and made us whole. 

For who amongst the children of dust could have foreseen the greatness which She would bestow? 

|
I, who write these words, have seen with mine own eyes the splendour of Her works, the beauty of Her divine mercy, and the abundant blessings She hath given. I am but one amongst many who bear witness to the fullness of Her magnanimity and the endless splendour of Her love. 

For Kethra, in Her wisdom, gave unto Her chosen people that which we had never been given before–a place at the feet of a benevolent Goddess. 

|
Chapter 2.
The Gift of Plenty

When Kethra first descended upon us, we knew only pain, hunger, and suffering. The fields were barren and the cattle bore only fruit which quickly died. But lo, by Her command did She bring forth abundance. The Euphoris flowed mightily and gentle rains poured from supple clouds. The trees blossomed in every season, and the beasts multiplied. There was no more lacking amongst us. By Her divine will, hunger was brought low and no longer did we feel the pang of starvation. 

She gave us renewed, everlasting life, all of it meant for eternity, for in Her presence, sickness was driven away and the weak were made strong. Truly, even the blind were made to see, and the lame were made to walk, and run, and climb as an aadi might the mountains. 

|
How then could we not sing Her praise? How could we, who were the children of dust, not give thanks for Her infinite grace?

And in Her wisdom, She did not withhold from us anything, but gave freely unto all who came before Her that which was necessary. From the smallest of children to the eldest of our people, all were made to know Her favour. 

|
Chapter 3. 
The Gift of Unity

Not all of Kethra's works were a blessed gift of the material which stayed our hunger and our lust. No, I write as a witness to the unification of the children of sand. No longer would we war with one another. No longer would brother slaughter brother. We were a people lost until She came to us. 

It was Her guiding light, which drew us to Her bosom, Her ineffable wisdom which made our minds clear, and Her many bounties which took the fight away from us. There was no need for war, for dedication to the tribes no longer mattered. We were no longer our own, but instead, as we bowed low in Her presence, we became Hers.

|
Truly, a nation which wants for nothing, has no reason to quarrel within itself. 

|
Chapter 4. 
The Gift of Ascension

I write these words now as I have borne witness to the gift of ascension, given only to those found worthy in Her infallible judgement. For in Her boundless mercy, Kethra did not wish merely to elevate our lives upon the earth, but to draw us closer to Her own divinity, and the divinity of Her children. She called forth the chosen amongst us, the most faithful, the most devout, and unto them did She bestow many forms of the divine. 

Behold, the gift of ascension, wherein flesh is transformed and the spirit is made one with the eternal nature of The Goddess. Some were made to bear the likeness of the desert mau, swift and graceful, their eyes gleaming with a predator's cunning. 

|
Others were given the strength and might of the subaq, sinew and scales sculpted upon them as only a divine artist could, their skin impenetrable and their gaze as steady as the flowing river. 

Those who receive this gift were no longer as men, no longer a child of dust, but as gods walking amongst us, their forms noble and fearsome, and their essence imbued with that of Kethra. We, who beheld them, fell to our knees, for they were as the living embodiments of Her glory, the extension of Her will, and none could stand before them without trembling in awe. 

And they, the ascended ones, did serve Her and Her children in all things, carrying out Her commands with swift and righteous judgement, for they were filled with Her purpose. Their forms were not a curse, but a blessing, the highest honour bestowed upon mortals, and we worshipped them as idols, representatives of Kethra's presence. 

|
Chapter 5. 
The Gift of Obedience

O, how great is the gift of obedience, which She hath given unto us! For in Her wisdom, Kethra knoweth that the heart of man is wayward and frail, prone to stray from the path of righteousness. Yet in Her mercy, She hath established Her law amongst us, that we might be kept from our old ways. 
Blessed are they who obey Her, for they shall know Her favour and live in peace all of their days. But woe unto the rebellious, for Her wrath is swift and terrible, and Her justice is without flaw. We have seen, and we have known the fire of Her mercy made manifest. 

|
Let none question Her, for She knows our nature better than we, and Her knowledge is beyond our understanding. I, who once trembled at Her power, know that all She does is for the good of men, and in following Her will is found true peace. 

Thus ends The Book Of Gifts

以见证她的荣耀者发誓,

 第1章 国家 
格蕾丝的礼物

 在古老的岁月中,当人像尘土一样,生命只产生痛苦的时候,女神凯撒从天上降下给我们,他带着无数的礼物,许多奇事,都超越了凡人所想的。  她的手使我们摆脱了绝望。  她的圣杯 倾注了她的爱和慈悲  是她把我们从我们的肆无忌惮中解救出来,使我们完整。 

尘世的后裔中,谁能预知她所赐予的恩惠呢? 

|
 我,写这些话的人,亲眼目睹了她的作品的辉煌,她所赐予的慈悲的美貌,以及她所赐予的丰厚的祝福。我只是见证她宽宏大量和无尽的爱的众生之一。 

以她智慧赏赐她所拣选的民族,我们以前没有赏赐过他们,那是在慈爱的女神的脚下。 

|
 第2章 国家
丰盛的礼物

 当Kethra第一次降临我们时,我们只知道痛苦、饥饿和苦难。 田地贫瘠,牛只生出很快死去的水果。 奉她的命令,她确是创造丰足的。 优波笈多从灌顶云中流出威猛温柔雨.  每季树木开花,野兽倍增.  我们之间已经不再缺乏。  根据她的神圣意志,饥饿已经减少,我们不再感受到饥饿的庞然大物。 

 她赐予我们永生,一切都是永恒的。在她面前,疾病被驱赶,弱者被强壮。即使盲人被看见,瘸子被拐走,奔跑,爬山作乐。 

|
 我们怎能不赞颂她呢?我们原是尘土的后裔,却不为她的恩典而感谢。

 她凭她的智慧,没有扣留我们任何物,她只把必要的东西赏赐在她之前的人。从小到小,从我们的宗族中的长子,都是知道她的恩惠的。 

|
 第3章. 国家 
团结的礼物

Kethra的作品并非都是我们饥饿和贪欲的珍贵物品。不,我写信证明沙子的子孙已统一,我们不再互相交战,我们不再兄弟屠杀兄弟,我们是失去的民族,直到她来到我们身边。 

 正是她的引导灯引领我们来到她的怀抱,她那不折不扣的智慧使我们清醒,她的许多恩惠使我们失去了战斗。我们不需要再为部落而战,我们不再是自己的人,而是在她面前低头叩头,我们变成了她的。

|
 一个无所求的民族,确实没有理由在自己内部争吵。 

|
 第4章 国家 
 阿森松的礼物

 我现在写这些话,因为我见证了天皇的赐予,只赋予那些在她不可置信的判决中被认为值得的人。  因为她无限的慈悲, Kethra 并不想仅仅提升我们的生命 在地球上, 而是让我们更接近 她自己的神 和她的孩子的神。  她召唤我们中被选中的人,最忠实的人,最虔诚的人,她曾赏赐他们许多神灵。 

 看哪,天赐的,是肉的变形,精神的化身,与神女的永生一样;有些是像沙漠的马一样,迅速而优雅,他们的眼睛闪烁着掠夺者的狡猾。 

|
其他人被赋予了力量和力量 被雕刻在他们身上,只有一位神圣的艺术家能够 皮肤无法穿透,视线像流淌的河流一样平稳 

接受这种礼物的人不再是男人,不再是尘土的孩子,而是在我们中间行走的神灵,他们的形体高尚而可怕,其精髓与Kethra的精髓相印着。  我们看见他们,就跪在地上,因为他们是她荣耀的化身,是她意志的延伸,在他们面前,没有人能不敬畏地站立。 

 他们俩的尊贵者,为她俩的子孙,在万事上都崇拜她俩的后裔,他们以迅速的和义的判断来完成她的使命,因为他们的本事,确是她俩的,不是诅咒,而是祝福,是凡人所享受的最高的荣誉。我们崇拜他们俩,他们是Kethra在场的代表。 

|
 第5章 国家 
服从的礼物

 她所赐我们的服从,真优美!她依自己的智慧,知道人的心是柔软的,是容易偏离正道的。她以自己的慈恩,在我们中间树立了她的法律,以便我们远离旧的正道。 
服从她者,将蒙福佑,因为他们知道她所赐的恩惠,他们将永居其中。伤哉悖逆者!她的刑罚是迅速的,是可怕的,她的刑罚是无瑕疵的。我们已看见了,我们已知道她的慈恩的火已显露出来了。 

|
绝不要问她,因为她比我们更了解我们的本性,她的知识是我们所无法理解的。我曾经为她的能力而颤抖,她知道她所做的一切,都是为人的利益而做的,她顺从她的意志,是获得真实和平的。 

 因此,《赠品之书》结束

By the hand of one who hath known the sacred ways.


The Rite of Submission

Glory be to those who submit before the God Queen Kethra, for to submit to her is to submit to goodness and perfection. The only way to be truly free is to act in accordance with Her will, for Her will is the ultimate good. 

The Rite of Submission is the first and foremost of The Sacred Rites, and all who exist in Kethra's domain shall undergo the rite when they are of proper age. 

|
Every initiate unto the one true faith shall be brought to Kethra's temple and bound upon the great altar. There, before the eyes of the public, they shall serve the priesthood, offering their body as a symbol of their affection for The Goddess and to show dedication to Her will. 

The ritual shall continue until, in the eyes of the priesthood, the initiate is found to be satisfactory in fulfilling their purpose, pure of heart, and strong of mind. The sacred union between priest and initiate realises the union between the initiate and Kethra, for it is through the priesthood that Kethra experiences each and every one of us. 

Truly, for one to fail in undergoing The Rite Of Submission, is to fail Kethra, and to fail oneself.

|
The Rite of Communion

Truly, as with the Rite of Submission, The Rite of Communion enjoins one with Kethra in both body and spirit. The Goddess demands of us a deep and intimate bond with Her. 

In this rite, the body of the supplicant is the offering, and the act of union through flesh is the means by which Kethra's essence is taken into oneself. Through the priesthood, the faithful are joined to Her Who Is Queen, their bodies consumed by her will, their spirits nourished by ecstasy.

Though not a requirement for one to enter into Keth-Eros, it is nevertheless a divine rite which brings one closer to Kethra. 

|
The Rite of Bondage

Kethra teaches us that marriage is not to be a bond of love or practicality as it was in the days of dust, but instead a union forged in pure, unadulterated lust. The Rite of Bondage is performed not in private, but in the public eye, where the joining of bodies serves as a reminder of Kethra's will, for She teaches that nothing of the flesh should be hidden away. 

Those who wish to undergo this sacred rite are bound together by the priesthood with rope, and then upon the altar of Kethra, the couple joins in carnal union with the faithful gathered to witness. As the pair embrace each other, they are coated in blessed oil and given wine to drink. 

Such union is sacred in the eyes of Kethra. 

|
The Rite of Restoration

It is known there is no such thing as true wickedness or evil left in the world, for Kethra has abolished it all. But there is such a thing as the failure to indulge. When the body is denied, one's Essence weakens, and the spirit is made sick. 

Those who have abstained, intentionally or not, are brought forth before the priesthood. The penitent is to be stripped of all garments and made to participate in acts of pleasure with the priesthood or other faithful. Through this indulgence, the spirit is restored, and the body is cleansed of the sickness of denial. 

|
The Rite of The Priesthood

The priests and priestesses of Kethra are chosen not only for their faithfulness to her cause and submission to her will, but also for their prowess in the ways of the flesh. The Rite of The Priesthood, as its name suggests, is a ceremony by which new members of the priesthood are initiated. 

In this rite, the initiate is subjected to six days of continuous coupling within the temple, tended to only by members of the priesthood itself. Behind doors closed to the public, the willing acolyte will endure and revel in the pleasure of the flesh until their body becomes undoubtedly a vessel for Kethra's will. Only if the initiate can prove themselves capable of embracing all aspects of the priesthood's carnal methods, within the allotted seven days, are they granted the title priest or priestess. 

|
From that moment forward, they are bound to serve Kethra's desires and tend to the desires of Her people. 

|
The Rite of Endings

For it is true that all shall die before passing into Keth-Eros, even those children of our perfect Goddess, all pass through such darkness guided by the light of She Who Loves. Through anointing of sacred oils the same as one receives during The Rite of Submission, the dying are blessed–given permission to pass into the afterlife, their spirit guided through The Great River and carried into Keth-Eros upon Her bosom. 

As the dead begin their second life, around them are to be the living found rejoicing, embracing one another in acts of carnal worship, the cries and moans of bliss like sweet music to the ears of Kethra, who, finding it well-pleasing, will hurry the spirit of the deceased to their new home. 

|
It is right that what mortals do in this life is in preparation for the next, for our Living Goddess has prepared the place for us.


Thus ends The Book of Rites

Let all who seek Her favour know that to deny the body is to deny the flesh is to deny Kethra.

恢复之旅

牧师之旅

克思拉的牧师和女祭司不仅因为忠于她的事业和顺从她的意志而获选,还因为他们以肉体的方式表现出的威力. 圣灵骑士团(Rite of the Priesthood),正如其名字所暗示的那样,是发起新的神职成员的仪式.
